text: When working with APIs, developers use HTTP requests to ask for or send data. Most modern APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy for computers and humans to read. Before making requests, you often need authentication—usually an API key—to verify who you are. Many services also have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests in a given time period; going over this may temporarily block you. Error handling is essential: always check the response status codes (like 404 or 500) and provide clear messages for failures. Understanding these basics helps you build reliable applications that communicate smoothly with external services.
